Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Emergency: brief retention window for live triage

Hi Kimberly,

We’re in the middle of a production incident affecting our reconciliation pipeline (FinOptima account). Our engineers need a short retention carveout to preserve request/response logs and KV caches from 2027-05-09 04:00-09:00 PDT while we triage root cause.

What we need:
- Preserve full token-level request/response traces and KV cache snapshots for the 5-hour window above
- Access for two FinOptima engineers and one Redwood SRE for live replay
- A 72-hour hold period (after which data should be auto-deleted)

I’ve attached a sample of the trace and the triage access request form. Please let me know what approvals you need from your side; our legal and security teams are on standby.

Thanks,
Samira

Samira — thanks for the details and the sample trace.

Quick clarifying Qs before I escalate for approval:
- Exact list of external engineer emails that need access (we limit temporary credentials per-person)
- Is the data strictly needed in US region or can we move a copy to an encrypted EU bucket during triage?
- Can you confirm you only need read-only replay access (no model weight changes or export of customer PII)

My proposed approach from Redwood side (to minimize scope):
- Limit retention exception to 48 hours by default; extend to 72 only with explicit signoff from FinOptima security
- Issue time-limited, role-scoped credentials for the named engineers and one Redwood SRE
- Snapshot KV cache into an encrypted, access-audited object (we will record token-level access logs for audit)

I’ll need Marcus (Legal) and Monica (Security) to sign off on the carveout and the access list. Looping them in.

—Kimberly

Team — forwarding FinOptima’s request. Key points:
- Preserve logs + KV cache for a 5-hour production window (started 04:00 PDT)
- FinOptima requests 72 hours; they’ll accept 48 if we prefer that as a control
- Access list: rajiv.patel@finoptima.com, emily.cho@finoptima.com, plus one Redwood SRE
- Residency: MUST remain in US (FinOptima constraint)

Suggested mitigations we can enforce:
1) Limit the carveout to specific object prefixes and start/end timestamps.
2) Issue per-user ephemeral creds that expire at the end of the carveout.
3) Enable enhanced audit logging and export logs to a sealed bucket for compliance.
4) Auto-delete after X hours (decide 48 vs 72).

Questions for Marcus: is 48 hours acceptable as a standard emergency carveout, or do we need documented legal signoff for 72-hour holds? If yes, what form do you want the customer to sign?

This is time-sensitive — FinOptima is blocking a reconciliation cutover. They asked for action within the hour.

—Kimberly

Kimberly / team — I approve a 48-hour timeboxed retention exception with the following conditions:
- Explicit list of external individuals (we have rajiv.patel@finoptima.com and emily.cho@finoptima.com on thread) — no additional ad-hoc additions without reopening approval
- Data must remain in US region; no cross-region copies unless redacted and legally approved
- Read-only replay only; export of PII is prohibited. Any derived/anonymized metrics must be pre-cleared by FinOptima security and recorded in the waiver doc
- We must capture an audit bundle (who/when/what) and attach to the FinOptima folder for retention of the waiver and the decision trail

Action items for operations (Monica / Laura):
- Implement scoped snapshot and ephemeral creds now; set auto-delete at 48h from snapshot timestamp
- Upload audit bundle and waiver to the FinOptima compliance folder and notify legal@example.redwood (for recordkeeping)

If FinOptima insists on 72 hours, we can do that but require an executed waiver (DocuSign) before extending beyond 48h.

—Marcus
